title: Disable tracking for a calculation
summary: torch.no_grad runs operations without building a gradient-tracking graph. This is useful when you only need predictions.
introduction: torch.no_grad runs operations without building a gradient-tracking graph. This is useful when you only need predictions. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain disable tracking for a calculation
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: torch.no_grad runs operations without building a gradient-tracking graph. This is useful when you only need predictions.

blocks.code:
import torch

x = torch.tensor(3.0, requires_grad=True)
with torch.no_grad():
    y = x * 2
print(y.requires_grad)
blocks.title: Disable tracking for a calculation

blocks.text: The result is False. The output is not tracked for a backward calculation.
